surface.$description: Page structure — canvas, cards/panels, recessed fields, backdrops. page and default are both literal white deliberately — cards read as 'raised' via border.default, not a background shift. Use default/page for the vast majority of the UI; sunken is for genuinely recessed elements only, used sparingly.

page.$description: Page canvas — the dominant background color across the whole product.

default.$description: Default raised surface — cards, panels. Same value as surface.page on purpose; separated from the page by border.default, not a darker background.

sunken.$description: Inputs, table row stripes, code blocks — recessed relative to a default surface. Reach for this rarely; it's the exception, not the norm.

overlay.$description: Modal/drawer backdrop scrim. The one legitimate opacity use in this system — it must composite over arbitrary page content, unlike bg.* tints which sit on a known surface.

inverse.$description: The one dark surface role in an otherwise light-themed system — Tooltip's background. Pair with text.onFill/icon.onFill (white), never text.default. Added 2026-07-21 for the overlay-family components; not a general 'dark mode' token, scoped to small inverse-context UI.

bg.$description: Passive status surfaces (banners, badges, notification chips) — solid light tints, not opacity. Pair with the matching text.* or icon.* color at the same role, never with text.default.

ai.$description: Added 2026-07-22 for Composer's AI Assist button — a genuine cross-product need (Message Center's composer and the future AI chat product both want a distinct 'this is the AI feature' accent), same bar surface.inverse was added under. violet was already an unused-as-semantic-role primitive family, picked over the 4 existing status roles on purpose — none of primary/success/danger/warning mean 'AI', reusing one would misattribute the feature to an unrelated status.

border.$description: Hairlines, dividers, and role-colored outlines. border.focus is always blue regardless of the focused element's own role.

default.$description: Default hairline — card edges, dividers, input borders at rest.

strong.$description: Emphasized divider, input border on hover.

focus.$description: Focus ring — always this color regardless of the focused element's own role.

text.$description: Content color. Role text (primary/success/danger/warning) sits at each family's 600 step — AA text-safe (≥4.5:1). muted is a deliberate exception, see its own note.

muted.$description: Placeholders, captions, timestamps — intentionally below AA text contrast (~3.9:1); never use for content the user must read to complete a task.

onFill.$description: Text/label sitting on a solid fill.* color (button labels, filled badges). Literal white, not a ramp step — none of the fill.* colors are dark enough to need anything else. Must be paired with semibold/bold weight: at fill's 500 step, contrast against white lands at 3.7-4.4:1 (large-text/UI-component AA, not the 4.5:1 small-text threshold) — checked directly, true for every role, not just one.

ai.$description: Pairs with bg.ai — same 600-step AA-safe convention every other text.* role already uses.

icon.$description: Mirrors text.* but one step lighter/less saturated where noted — icons are graphical elements (WCAG 3:1 UI-component rule), not small text (4.5:1), so role icons sit at each family's 500 step, not 600.

disabled.$description: Matches text.disabled — icon and label go equally quiet together on a disabled control.

ai.$description: Pairs with text.ai/bg.ai — same 500-step convention every other role icon already uses.

fill.$description: Solid, saturated backgrounds for interactive controls (buttons, checkboxes, toggles, filled badges) — pairs with text.onFill / icon.onFill, never with text.default. Label text on any fill.* must be semibold or bold — see text.onFill.

neutral.$description: Secondary/neutral button fill — pairs with text.default, not text.onFill (too light for white text).

ai.$description: Solid AI accent, for a hypothetical fully-filled AI button — Composer's own AI Assist button actually uses the pale bg.ai tint (see Composer's own tokens), not this; kept for parity with every other role having both a tint and a solid step available.

status.$description: Reserved state meaning (good/warning/danger/info) for badges, alerts, form validation. Never reuse a chart-series color for status, and never reuse status for 'series 4' — see tokens/primitives/chart-series.tokens.json's own rule. Always pair with an icon + label, not color alone.

avatar.$description: Categorical identity tints for Avatar's initials fallback — a person with no photo gets one of these 8 hues assigned deterministically (hash their name to a slot), so distinct people read as distinct colors across a list instead of every fallback avatar being the same gray. Same hue order and reasoning as tokens/primitives/chart-series.tokens.json (validated CVD-safe adjacency) but a separate token set on purpose: chart-series sits at the 500 step for saturated lines/bars on a white plot area, this sits at 100 (bg, pastel) / 600 (text, AA-safe — same step text.primary/success/danger/warning already use) for a quiet fallback badge, not a data mark. Don't reuse chart-series' own tokens here, and don't reuse these for charts.

tag.$description: Decorative, non-semantic categorical color for generic tagging/labeling (Badge's 'color' axis, e.g. a Notion/Linear/GitHub-style label picker) — deliberately separate from the 5 meaningful status roles (bg.*/fill.* primary/success/warning/danger + this group's own gray). Picking tag.orange means 'I want an orange label', not 'this is a warning'. Two intensities per hue: tint (pale bg + colored text, same 100/600 pairing bg.*/text.* already use) and solid (saturated bg + text.onFill, same 500-step + white pairing fill.* already uses) — same contrast trade-off already accepted for fill.primary/success/danger/warning (3.7-4.4:1 large-text/UI-component AA, not 4.5:1 small-text; pair with semibold/bold label weight). 4 of the 10 hues (blue/red/green/amber) are pure aliases of the existing primary/danger/success/warning role tokens, not new colors — 'color=blue' and 'role=primary' render identically on purpose, since blue already means primary/info everywhere else in this system. gray aliases role=neutral for tint only — see gray's own $description for why solid diverges. Only orange/violet/magenta/teal/brown are genuinely new leaf references. Same hue order as chart-series/avatar for one consistent categorical rhythm across the system.

gray.$description: The one hue that ISN'T a full role alias — tint matches role=neutral (bg.neutral/text.default) but solid diverges deliberately: fill.neutral (gray.100) is the same pale value as the tint bg, so a 'solid gray' badge built from it would look identical to the tint one, not actually filled. Uses color.gray.500 + text.onFill instead — the same saturated-500-step + white-text pattern every other solid hue already uses, gray included. role=neutral's own solid stays on fill.neutral/text.default on purpose (matches Button secondary's established pale-even-when-emphasized precedent) — a neutral *status* has no 'urgent solid' need the way a decorative gray *tag* does, so this is the one place role and color genuinely diverge rather than alias.
